Let's use a restaurant.

**The scene.** You're a diner. You can't walk into the kitchen. You never see the stove or the chef. What you have is:

- **A menu.** Each dish has a name and a short description, plus what the kitchen needs from you, like "steak: how done?" The menu is all you know about what the kitchen can do.
- **An order slip.** You write "Steak, medium" and nothing more. You don't cook the steak. You only say what you want.
- **A waiter.** The waiter takes your slip to the kitchen, gets the dish made, and brings the plate back to your table. Nothing reaches you except what the waiter carries.

You look at the plate and decide what to do next. You might order dessert, send the steak back, or say "that's all, thanks." The meal ends when you decide it's over, or when the restaurant closes.

**The general idea.** Tool calling works the same way. The model is the diner. It reads the menu (the descriptions of the tools) and writes a slip. It never touches the kitchen. Everything the kitchen actually does happens outside the model, and the model only sees what comes back to it.

**Where the analogy breaks.** A diner remembers the whole meal. A model only knows what's written on the page it's handed each time, so the earlier slips and plates have to be put back in front of it.

**Your turn.** Map the pieces onto your makerspace assistant. What is the menu, the slip, the waiter and the kitchen? And who decides what happens after the plate arrives? Try it in your own words and I'll tell you what's right and what's off.

I'm leaving the mapping to you on purpose. Quiz 0001 tests this idea and hasn't been graded yet, so I can't settle its items for you. I'm happy to go through it item by item right after grading.
